notes: Confidence: observed -- the report lines, the four gcc commands, the case shapes and the valgrind clauses, all read from re/original-grade-txt/34_put_together.grade.txt; recovered -- the driver's check (compare each X.counts with X.ans, in the original's M,C,Y / C,M,Y line order) is reconstructed from those observed lines and validated by rebuilding the recorded solution, whose .counts files match every provided .ans except the '<unknown>' spacing; inferred -- that whitespace tolerance and the substitution of list1a.txt for the missing list3a.txt. Observed in re/original-grade-txt/34_put_together.grade.txt: the 'Attempting to compile:' header and the four gcc -c ... / gcc -o count_values lines; the '###...' separators and 'testcaseN:' numbering; 'testcase1 passed, your program successfully indicated a failure' for the error-checking case; 'Your file matched the expected output' / 'Comparing file list1a.txt.counts with answer' / 'Your output is correct' per compared file; '  - Valgrind was clean (no errors, no memory leaks)' / 'valgrind was clean'; 'Overall Grade: A'. The original was `make`-driven (count_values built from outname.o counts.o main.o kv.o with cards.c-style symlinks to 29_outname/32_kvs/33_counts), so the build compiles the same four sources separately in the same order; the commands are echoed (showCompileCommands) but clang spells them slightly differently and prefixes temp paths, so those lines differ from 2024's. The driver wraps the student's own main (-Dmain=student_main) so the program under test is the student's real program, and per case it deletes X.counts before the run (a stale file must not look like a pass), then compares X.counts with X.ans -- 'answer' in the original's own wording, and the file the README names for list1a/list1b/list2a-c. The comparison ignores whitespace runs because the recorded solution prints '<unknown>: 2' where list1a.txt.ans says '<unknown> : 2' (verified by rebuilding the recorded solution: the only difference from every provided .ans is that space, and 33_counts.grade.txt shows the 2024 grader accepting the same difference against the README's '<unknown> : 1' format). Nothing else is normalised. CASE 4 IS A SUBSTITUTE: the original compared 'list3a.txt.counts' and list3a.txt is not in the workspace (only list1a/1b, list2a/b/c and test.txt exist; test.txt has no .ans), so the single-file shape is reproduced with list1a.txt. memory_check matches the original exactly here -- valgrind clauses appear in this grade.txt -- so leaks and memory errors are real failures. Message fields reproduce the original's first line after each 'testcaseN:'; the tool still appends its own 'testcaseN passed'. Neither engine reports uninitialised reads, which valgrind did, so that class of defect is not detected here.
